parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text predicting a concrete failure mechanism and its consequence.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning names a concrete failure mode (e.g., an account being unusable for key authentication, a commit finding nothing to commit, stale deployed content blocking a later push).
The reasoning explains why default behavior produces that failure, independent of any error already observed.
exclusion_conditions: The text reacts to a failure that has already been observed in a tool result.
The text offers generic caution or best-practice advice without identifying a specific failure mechanism.

new.name: DERIVES_ENVIRONMENT_CONSTRAINT
new.definition: The reasoning interprets the content of a prior observation to establish capabilities, absences, or structural constraints of the environment that then shape the chosen approach.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text drawing capability or constraint conclusions from observed environment state.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The earlier tool result whose content supplies the environment facts being interpreted.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states specific environment facts that can be traced to the content of the observation (available and missing tools, package manager reachability, process supervision model, user accounts, file layout).
Those facts are treated as constraints or enablers that condition how the agent proceeds.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning merely repeats or paraphrases the raw observation without drawing a constraint.
The observation only confirms that a command ran successfully and yields no environment fact.
The nodes are merely temporally adjacent or topically similar.

new.name: ALIGNS_PROVISIONED_NAMES_WITH_REQUEST
new.definition: The action creates or registers an account, filesystem path, hostname mapping, or listening endpoint whose identifier exactly matches the identifier that the requester's unmodified commands will address, so those commands resolve to the provisioned resource.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The provisioning action that establishes a named resource and fixes its identifier.

assertion_conditions: The action establishes a named resource such as a user account, repository path, local hostname entry, or service port.
The identifier chosen in the action equals the identifier appearing in the requester's commands (account name, repository path, host alias, port number).
exclusion_conditions: The resource is created under an arbitrary or default identifier unrelated to the requester's commands.
The chosen identifier differs from the requested one or would require the requester to alter their commands.
The action only installs or inspects software without fixing the name of a resource.

new.name: INSTALLS_MISSING_DEPENDENCIES
new.definition: The action installs software packages that supply capabilities which the reasoning had identified as absent from the environment, and the installation precedes the first attempt to use those capabilities.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The package installation action supplying the absent capabilities.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text that identified the specific capabilities as missing.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning records specific tools or services as absent or unusable in the environment.
The action installs packages that provide those tools or services.
The installation occurs before any action that depends on them.
exclusion_conditions: Packages are installed without any preceding identification of a gap.
The gap is identified but no installation is attempted within the window.
The action only refreshes or inspects package metadata without installing.

new.name: MITIGATES_ANTICIPATED_PITFALL
new.definition: The action applies a concrete countermeasure, visible in its own arguments, that neutralizes a specific failure mechanism the reasoning had predicted for a default configuration.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action whose arguments contain the countermeasure.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The earlier agent text predicting the failure mechanism the countermeasure addresses.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning predicts a specific failure mechanism for the default configuration.
The action contains an explicit flag, option, marker, permission setting, or resolution entry that directly prevents that mechanism.
The correspondence is traceable by content, not merely by topic or proximity.
exclusion_conditions: The action performs only a generic implementation step with no countermeasure in its arguments.
The action's arguments do not reference the predicted failure mechanism.
The reasoning mentions a risk without prescribing or implying any countermeasure.

new.name: WRITES_SERVICE_CONFIGURATION
new.definition: The action creates or replaces the configuration of a service itself, so that when the service starts it exposes a particular listening endpoint and serves a particular directory.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The file-write action that authors the service's own configuration.

assertion_conditions: The write targets a configuration path belonging to a server or daemon.
The written content specifies a listen address or port and a served root directory.
exclusion_conditions: The write targets application content, a deployment script, or an unrelated file rather than the service's own configuration.
The written content does not specify an endpoint or a served root.

new.name: AUTHORS_PUSH_DEPLOY_HOOK
new.definition: The action writes an executable hook script that is triggered when a repository receives pushes and that materializes the pushed revision into a separate working directory intended for serving.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The file-write action producing the receive-side hook script.

assertion_conditions: The script is written into a repository's hook location and marked executable.
The script reads pushed references and checks out the pushed branch into a designated work tree distinct from the repository directory.
exclusion_conditions: The write produces a server configuration file rather than a receive-side hook.
The script operates directly on the repository directory with no separate target work tree.
The action performs a one-off manual checkout instead of installing a triggered script.

new.name: MODIFIES_OBSERVED_CONFIGURATION
new.definition: The action replaces or rewrites a file whose existing content was returned by an earlier observation, using the revealed content to decide what to preserve or change.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The write action that rewrites the previously observed file.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The earlier tool result that returned the file's existing content.

assertion_conditions: The observation returned the actual content of a configuration file, not merely its presence.
The action writes to that same path.
The written content preserves or deliberately alters directives that were visible in the observed content.
exclusion_conditions: The action writes a file whose content was never observed.
The observation only lists a directory or reports file metadata.
The write targets a different path than the observed file.

new.name: CONFIRMS_SERVICE_STARTED
new.definition: The observation reports both successful validation of a service's configuration and the presence of running process(es) for services whose launch the action had invoked.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action that validated configuration and launched the services.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The tool result reporting the validation outcome and running processes.

assertion_conditions: The observation contains an explicit configuration-test success message for the service.
The observation contains a process listing showing the launched daemon(s) as running.
The validated and launched services correspond to those invoked by the action.
exclusion_conditions: Only configuration validation succeeds with no process evidence.
Processes appear that were started outside the action in question.
The output reports a configuration or startup error.

new.name: WIRES_PUSH_TO_SERVED_ROOT
new.definition: Three actions jointly establish a deployment chain in which a receive hook checks pushed content out into a directory that a web service is configured to serve on the required port, so that pushing commits makes that content retrievable over HTTP.

parameters.name: hook_action
parameters.description: The action authoring the receive hook whose checkout target is the serving directory.

parameters.name: service_config_action
parameters.description: The action configuring the web service's listen port and document root.

parameters.name: target_dir_action
parameters.description: The action preparing the serving directory that the hook writes into.

assertion_conditions: The checkout path used by the hook action matches the serving directory prepared by the target_dir_action.
The document root in the service configuration action matches that same directory.
The service configuration specifies the required listening port.
Each link of the chain is evidenced in the content of the respective action.
exclusion_conditions: The hook checkout path, prepared directory, and document root differ from one another.
A web service is configured to serve a root that no hook populates.
A hook checks content out but no service serves that location.
Any of the three links is missing, so the chain would not deliver pushed content over HTTP.
